differential_candidates.differentiator: Crushing retrosternal pressure, diaphoresis, radiating to left arm/jaw
Burning sensation after meals, relieved by antacids, no radiation
Reproducible on chest wall palpation, exacerbated by deep inspiration

formulary_guidelines.standard_dose: 300 mg chewed/dispersed once as emergency first-aid loading dose
formulary_guidelines.contraindications: Active GI bleeding, known hypersensitivity to salicylates
formulary_guidelines.telemedicine_status: Emergency loading dose pending physical hospital transfer

formulary_guidelines.standard_dose: 5 mg sublingually if systolic BP > 100 mmHg
formulary_guidelines.contraindications: Hypotension (SBP < 90), concurrent use with PDE-5 inhibitors

guidelines: POSSIBLE MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION OR CARDIOVASCULAR EMERGENCY. TIME IS MUSCLE. DO NOT DELAY.
action_plan:
1. Administer emergency medical services immediately. Call 108 or 112 (India).
2. Keep patient calm, seated, or in a half-reclined position.
3. Assist with emergency dispersible aspirin (300mg) if advised by emergency dispatch and no contraindication.
4. Prepare for immediate transfer to a cardiac catheterization center.

differential_candidates.differentiator: Expiratory wheezing, history of atopy/allergies
Sudden onset, pleuritic chest pain, tachycardia, DVT history
Unilateral chest pain, absent breath sounds on affected side

formulary_guidelines.standard_dose: 100 mcg per puff; 2-4 puffs via spacer every 20 minutes as rescue for acute bronchospasm

guidelines: ACUTE BREATHING EMERGENCY. RISK OF RESPIRATORY FAILURE.
action_plan:
1. Call ambulance services (108 / 112) immediately.
2. Keep patient sitting upright; loosen restrictive clothing.
3. Administer rescue bronchodilator (Salbutamol 2-4 puffs) if diagnosed with asthma.
4. Keep supplemental oxygen ready if available.

differential_candidates.differentiator: Sudden focal neurological deficit, unilateral weakness, slurred speech
Sudden severe 'thunderclap' headache, vomiting, rapid loss of consciousness
Focal symptoms resolving completely within 24 hours

recommended_investigations: Non-Contrast CT Brain (NCCT Head) immediately (<20 min door-to-CT)
Blood Glucose (Rule out severe hypoglycemia mimicking stroke)
guidelines: ACUTE STROKE ALERT. TIME IS BRAIN. THROMBOLYSIS WINDOW (<4.5 HOURS).
action_plan:
1. Call 108 / 112 immediately. Note exact time of symptom onset.
2. Check FAST: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call.
3. Do NOT administer any food, water, or aspirin orally (choking/hemorrhage risk).
4. Position patient in recovery position if consciousness is decreased.

differential_candidates.differentiator: Pulsatile bright red blood spurt
Continuous dark red blood flow

guidelines: SEVERE HEMORRHAGE. IMMEDIATE RISK OF HYPOVOLEMIC SHOCK.
action_plan:
1. Apply firm, continuous direct pressure with sterile pad.
2. Elevate bleeding site above heart level.
3. Call 108 / 112 emergency services.
4. Keep patient warm to avoid hypothermia.

differential_candidates.differentiator: Fever with mild coryza, body aches, no localizing signs
Retro-orbital headache, severe arthralgia ('breakbone'), petechial rash
Periodic chills, rigors, and sweating spikes, endemic travel history

recommended_investigations: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with Differential and Platelet Count
Dengue NS1 Antigen (if fever < 5 days) / IgM (if > 5 days)
Malaria Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT) / Peripheral Blood Smear
Urine Routine & Microscopy (if urinary symptoms present)

formulary_guidelines.standard_dose: 500 mg - 650 mg orally every 6-8 hours as needed (Maximum 3000 mg/day)
formulary_guidelines.contraindications: Severe hepatic impairment, active acute liver disease
formulary_guidelines.telemedicine_status: List A (Permissible for all telemedicine consultations)

formulary_guidelines.standard_dose: 1 sachet dissolved in 1 litre of clean drinking water; sip frequently
formulary_guidelines.contraindications: Severe intractable vomiting, dynamic intestinal obstruction

guidelines: EVALUATE FEVER PATTERN, HYDRATION, AND WARNING SIGNS.
action_plan:
1. Maintain hydration (ORS, coconut water, water).
2. Lukewarm water sponging for high temperature.
3. Paracetamol 500-650mg for symptom relief (max 3-4 times daily).
4. Seek immediate doctor visit if fever > 103°F (39.4°C), lasts >3 days, or if rash, petechiae, or severe vomiting occurs.

differential_candidates.differentiator: Self-limiting cough, clear/white phlegm, no focal crackles on auscultation
Throat clearing, sensation of mucus dripping down posterior pharynx
High fever, rust-colored or purulent sputum, pleuritic chest pain, tachypnea

recommended_investigations: Chest X-Ray (PA View) if cough persists > 2 weeks or with fever/hemoptysis

formulary_guidelines.standard_dose: Inhale steam 2-3 times daily; warm saline gargles every 4 hours
10 mg - 20 mg (5-10 ml) orally every 6-8 hours
formulary_guidelines.contraindications: Productive wet cough (do not suppress sputum), concurrent MAOI use

guidelines: SUPPORTIVE CARE FOR ACUTE VIRAL BRONCHITIS. AVOID EMPIRIC ANTIBIOTICS.
action_plan:
1. Steam inhalation and warm fluids (ginger-honey water).
2. Warm saline gargles to relieve airway sensitivity.
3. Avoid dusty/smoky environments.
4. Consult a doctor if cough lasts > 2 weeks, produces blood, or causes shortness of breath.

differential_candidates.differentiator: Watery loose stools, nausea, cramping, low-grade fever
Epigastric burning, aggravated on empty stomach
Initial periumbilical pain migrating to Right Lower Quadrant with McBurney tenderness

recommended_investigations: Stool Routine & Microscopy (check for RBCs, pus cells, ova/cysts)
Ultrasound Whole Abdomen (if localized severe right lower quadrant pain)

formulary_guidelines.standard_dose: 200-400 ml after each loose stool to prevent dehydration
40 mg orally once daily 30 minutes before breakfast for gastritis/acidity

guidelines: PREVENT DEHYDRATION FIRST. DO NOT PRESCRIBE EMPIRIC ANTIBIOTICS FOR UNCOMPLICATED DIARRHEA.
action_plan:
1. Aggressive oral rehydration with WHO-ORS solution.
2. Bland diet (Khichdi, bananas, boiled potatoes, toast).
3. Avoid self-prescribed antimicrobials or antimotility drugs (like Loperamide) in fever/bloody stool.
4. Consult a doctor promptly if signs of dehydration, high fever, or severe right-side abdominal pain develop.

differential_candidates.differentiator: Associated cough, rhinorrhea, conjunctivitis, mild pharyngeal erythema
Centor criteria: fever, tonsillar exudates, tender anterior cervical adenopathy, NO cough

recommended_investigations: Rapid Antigen Detection Test (RADT) for Group A Strep (if Centor score >= 3)

formulary_guidelines.standard_dose: 1/2 tsp salt in 200 ml warm water; gargle 4 times daily
500 mg orally every 8 hours as needed for throat pain

guidelines: SYMPTOMATIC RELIEF FOR VIRAL PHARYNGITIS. EVALUATE CENTOR CRITERIA FOR BACTERIAL STREP.
action_plan:
1. Warm saline gargles every 3-4 hours.
2. Lozenges and warm fluids.
3. Paracetamol for throat pain.
4. Consult doctor if unable to swallow liquids, breathing difficulty, or white patches on tonsils appear.
